q: By February 28, 2027, Benjamin Netanyahu is prime minister of a new Israeli government that has won a Knesset vote of confidence (remaining prime minister of a caretaker government because no new government is formed does not count)
basis: In three early-October polls (Kan, September 28; Zman Yisrael, September 30–October 1; Channel 12, October 6), Netanyahu's coalition bloc won 49–53 seats, 8–12 short of a 61-seat majority. The opposition, too, has 49–54 seats without the Arab parties (12–13 seats), making a majority hard to reach on its own. In the 2022 election Netanyahu's bloc won 64 seats, about four more than the final polling average of 60.3, but this time it would have to overturn a larger gap. If neither side can form a government, as in 2019–2021, Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister, but that outcome counts as a no for this forecast. With all votes counted in the October 27 election, Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19. The official results were presented to President Herzog on November 4. After consulting the parties, the president will choose whom to task with forming a government (the legal deadline is seven days after the official results).
rs: The Knesset's announcement of the confidence vote result
